name: Red Lentil Soup
description: A classic, creamy Turkish soup made with red lentils.
steps: Dice the onion, carrot, and potato into small cubes.
Sauté the vegetables in butter, then stir in the flour.
Add the lentils and 1.5 litres of water, and simmer for 25 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Blend until smooth, season with cumin and salt, and serve hot.

name: Ezogelin Soup
description: A spiced soup of red lentils, rice, and bulgur.
steps: Sauté the onion in butter and stir in the tomato paste.
Add the lentils, rice, bulgur, and water, and stir to combine.
Simmer over low heat for 30 minutes until everything is tender.
Season with mint, chili flakes, and salt, then serve.

name: Imam Bayildi
description: Aubergines stuffed with a sweet onion filling and slow-cooked in olive oil.
steps: Peel the aubergines and fry or roast until soft.
Sauté the onion, garlic, and tomato in olive oil to make the filling.
Split the aubergines open and stuff with the filling.
Drizzle with water and olive oil, then bake for 25 minutes and serve cold.

name: Karniyarik (Split-Belly Aubergine)
description: Aubergines stuffed with a minced meat filling and baked in the oven.
steps: Peel the aubergines, fry them, then slit them open lengthwise.
Brown the minced meat with onion and garlic, then add tomato and seasoning.
Fill the aubergines with the mixture and top with tomato and pepper slices.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 25 minutes.

name: Turkish Manti (Dumplings)
description: Tiny meat-filled dumplings served with garlicky yoghurt and melted butter.
steps: Knead a firm dough from flour, egg, salt, and water, then let it rest.
Mix the minced meat and onion to make the filling.
Roll the dough thin, cut into small squares, fill, and pinch closed.
Boil until cooked, then serve with garlicky yoghurt and melted butter sauce.

name: Olive Oil Stuffed Vine Leaves
description: Vine leaves rolled around a rice and herb filling.
steps: Sauté the onion in olive oil, then add the rice, currants, and pine nuts.
Season the filling with herbs and spices and cook briefly.
Place a small amount of filling on each leaf and roll up tightly.
Arrange in a pot and simmer with water and lemon juice for 35 minutes over low heat.

name: Menemen (Turkish Scrambled Eggs)
description: A quick Turkish breakfast of eggs cooked with tomato and pepper.
steps: Sauté the peppers in olive oil.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until the liquid reduces.
Crack in the eggs and cook, stirring gently or leaving them softly set.
Season with salt and chili flakes and serve hot.

name: Izmir-Style Meatballs
description: Baked meatballs with potatoes in a tomato sauce.
steps: Knead the minced meat with onion, garlic, bread, and egg, then shape into meatballs.
Lightly fry the meatballs.
Slice the potatoes and arrange in a baking dish, then place the meatballs on top.
Add tomato and pepper, and bake at 180°C (350°F) for 30 minutes.

name: Kisir (Bulgur Salad)
description: A refreshing salad of fine bulgur, tomato paste, and fresh herbs.
steps: Soak the bulgur in hot water and stir in the tomato and pepper pastes.
Once the bulgur has softened, add the chopped vegetables and herbs.
Toss with lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, and olive oil.
Chill in the fridge and serve cold.

name: Smoky Aubergine Salad
description: A traditional meze of smoky charred aubergine and yoghurt.
steps: Char-grill the aubergines and peel off the skins.
Chop the flesh and mix with crushed garlic and yoghurt.
Season with lemon juice and salt.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve cold.

name: Shepherd's Salad
description: A classic finely diced salad of tomato, cucumber, and pepper.
steps: Dice all the vegetables into small cubes.
Finely chop the parsley and add it in.
Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, and salt.
Transfer to a serving dish and serve right away.

name: Turlu (Mixed Vegetable Stew)
description: A hearty stew of seasonal vegetables cooked together in olive oil.
steps: Cut all the vegetables into large chunks.
Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil.
Add the remaining vegetables and toss for a few minutes.
Add the tomato and water, then simmer over low heat for 35 minutes.

name: Horiatiki (Greek Salad)
description: The classic Greek salad with feta cheese and olives.
steps: Roughly chop the tomato, cucumber, pepper, and onion.
Add the olives and a block of feta cheese.
Season with olive oil and oregano.
Add salt just before serving.

name: Moussaka
description: Layers of aubergine, spiced minced meat, and creamy béchamel, baked until golden.
steps: Slice the aubergine and potato and lightly fry.
Brown the minced meat with onion and tomato to make the sauce.
Make a béchamel sauce from butter, flour, and milk.
Layer the vegetables, meat sauce, and béchamel, then bake for 35 minutes.

name: Tzatziki
description: A cooling dip of strained yoghurt, cucumber, and garlic.
steps: Grate the cucumber and squeeze out the excess water.
Mix the yoghurt with crushed garlic and the cucumber.
Season with dill and salt.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve cold.

name: Spanakopita (Spinach Pie)
description: Layered filo pastry filled with spinach and feta cheese.
steps: Sauté the spinach with onion, then drain off any liquid.
Mix in the feta cheese, egg, and dill to make the filling.
Layer the filo sheets brushed with melted butter and the filling.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) until golden brown.

name: Chicken Souvlaki
description: Marinated chicken skewers, grilled and served with warm pita.
steps: Cube the chicken and marinate with olive oil, lemon, garlic, and oregano.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and grill or pan-fry.
Serve hot with warm pita bread.

name: Fasolada (Greek Bean Soup)
description: Greece's national soup, simmered with dried beans.
steps: Soak the dried beans overnight.
Sauté the vegetables in olive oil and stir in the tomato paste.
Add the beans and water and simmer until tender.
Season with salt and serve hot.

name: Gemista (Stuffed Tomatoes and Peppers)
description: Tomatoes and peppers baked with a rice and herb filling.
steps: Hollow out the tomatoes and peppers, reserving the flesh.
Mix the rice, onion, and herbs to make the filling.
Stuff the vegetables with the filling and arrange in a baking dish.
Drizzle with olive oil and bake for 40 minutes.

name: Pastitsio
description: A Greek baked pasta dish with minced meat sauce and béchamel.
steps: Boil the pasta until al dente.
Brown the minced meat with onion and tomato to make the sauce.
Make a béchamel sauce from butter, flour, and milk.
Layer the pasta, meat sauce, and béchamel, then bake.

name: Fava (Yellow Split Pea Purée)
description: A silky-smooth Greek meze made from yellow split peas.
steps: Simmer the split peas with onion until soft.
Blend until smooth.
Stir in the olive oil and lemon juice.
Serve warm or chilled.

name: Caprese Salad
description: A simple Italian salad of tomato, mozzarella, and basil.
steps: Slice the tomato and mozzarella.
Arrange the tomato, mozzarella, and basil leaves alternately on a plate.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Sprinkle with salt and serve immediately.

name: Minestrone
description: A hearty Italian soup of seasonal vegetables and pasta.
steps: Sauté the onion, carrot, and celery in olive oil.
Add the tomato and beans with water and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the courgette and pasta and cook until the pasta is done.
Season with salt and serve hot.

name: Bruschetta
description: Toasted bread topped with tomato and basil.
steps: Slice and toast the bread, then rub with garlic.
Dice the tomatoes and mix with basil.
Season with olive oil and salt.
Spoon the mixture over the toasted bread slices and serve.

name: Panzanella (Tuscan Bread Salad)
description: A Tuscan-style salad of stale bread and tomato.
steps: Cube the stale bread and lightly toast it.
Chop the tomato, cucumber, and onion.
Combine everything and add the basil.
Toss with olive oil, vinegar, and salt, then rest for 10 minutes.

name: Pasta alla Norma
description: A Sicilian pasta with aubergine and tomato sauce.
steps: Cube the aubergine and fry in olive oil.
Make a sauce with garlic and tomato, then add the aubergine.
Boil the pasta and toss with the sauce.
Top with cheese and basil, then serve.

name: Mushroom Risotto
description: A creamy Italian risotto of arborio rice and mushrooms.
steps: Sauté the mushrooms in butter and set aside.
Sauté the onion, then add the rice and stir until translucent.
Add the wine and hot stock gradually, stirring constantly.
Once the rice is cooked, stir in the mushrooms, butter, and parmesan.

name: Caponata
description: A sweet-and-sour Sicilian relish of aubergine, celery, and olives.
steps: Cube the aubergine and fry in olive oil.
Sauté the celery and onion separately.
Add the tomato, olives, and capers, and cook together.
Stir in the vinegar and cook for 5 more minutes, then serve cold.

name: Aglio e Olio
description: A simple Italian spaghetti with garlic and olive oil.
steps: Boil the spaghetti in salted water.
Gently cook the garlic in olive oil over low heat until lightly golden.
Add the chili flakes and toss with the cooked pasta.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

name: Margherita Pizza
description: The classic Italian pizza with tomato sauce, mozzarella, and basil.
steps: Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Scatter over the sliced mozzarella.
Bake in a preheated oven at high heat for 10 minutes.
Top with basil and a drizzle of olive oil, then serve.

name: Gazpacho
description: A chilled Spanish soup made from raw vegetables.
steps: Roughly chop all the vegetables.
Blend the vegetables with garlic, vinegar, and olive oil.
Season with salt and chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Serve cold.

name: Paella
description: Spain's famous saffron rice with chicken and seafood.
steps: Brown the chicken in olive oil and set aside.
Sauté the onion and tomato, then add the rice.
Add the hot saffron-infused stock and return the chicken to the pan.
In the final 10 minutes, add the prawns and mussels and continue cooking.

name: Patatas Bravas
description: Crispy fried potatoes with a spicy tomato sauce, a Spanish tapas classic.
steps: Cube the potatoes and fry or roast until crisp.
Make a sauce with garlic, tomato paste, and chili flakes.
Toss the fried potatoes with the sauce.
Serve hot.

name: Tortilla Española
description: A Spanish-style omelette made with potato and egg.
steps: Thinly slice the potato and onion and cook gently in plenty of olive oil until soft.
Beat the eggs and mix in the potatoes.
Cook in a pan, flipping to brown both sides.
Slice and serve warm.

name: Salmorejo
description: A thick, chilled Andalusian soup of tomato and bread.
steps: Roughly chop the tomatoes and blend with the bread.
Add the garlic, vinegar, and salt and blend again.
Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while blending until smooth.
Chill for at least 1 hour and serve cold.

name: Pisto
description: A Spanish-style vegetable medley of courgette, aubergine, and pepper.
steps: Cube all the vegetables.
Sauté the onion and pepper in olive oil.
Add the aubergine, courgette, and tomato, and cook over low heat.
Once the vegetables are soft, season with salt and serve.

name: Tabbouleh
description: A Levantine salad packed with fresh parsley and fine bulgur.
steps: Soak the bulgur in a little water and let it soften.
Finely chop the parsley, mint, tomato, and spring onion.
Combine the bulgur with the chopped ingredients.
Toss with lemon juice, olive oil, and salt, then serve.

name: Fattoush
description: A crisp Levantine salad topped with toasted pita.
steps: Break the pita into pieces and toast or fry until crisp.
Chop the vegetables and combine in a large bowl.
Make a dressing with pomegranate molasses, olive oil, sumac, and salt.
Toss in the toasted pita just before serving.

name: Baba Ganoush
description: A smoky Levantine dip of charred aubergine and tahini.
steps: Char the aubergines over a flame or in the oven.
Peel and mash the flesh.
Mix with tahini, lemon juice, and crushed garlic.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

name: Falafel
description: A Levantine classic of fried spiced chickpea patties.
steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight; do not boil before use.
Process the chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, and spices in a food processor.
Shape the mixture into small patties.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden brown.

name: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce.
steps: Sauté the onion, pepper, and garlic in olive oil.
Add the tomato and cumin and simmer until a thick sauce forms.
Make wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft.

name: Muhammara
description: A sweet-and-spicy Levantine dip of roasted red pepper and walnuts.
steps: Char-grill the red peppers and peel off the skins.
Process the peppers, walnuts, breadcrumbs, and pomegranate molasses together.
Stir in the chili flakes and salt.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

name: Hummus
description: A creamy Levantine dip of chickpeas and tahini.
steps: Blend the cooked chickpeas with their cooking liquid until smooth.
Add the tahini, lemon juice, and garlic, and blend again until creamy.
Season with cumin and salt.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

name: Manakish
description: Levantine flatbread topped with za'atar and olive oil.
steps: Knead the flour, yeast, salt, and water into a dough and let it rise for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into rounds and flatten them out.
Spread with the thyme and olive oil mixture.
Bake in a preheated oven for 10-12 minutes.

name: Warak Enab (Levantine Stuffed Vine Leaves)
description: Vine leaves rolled around a rice and herb filling, Levantine style.
steps: Mix the rice with chopped tomato and herbs to make the filling.
Place a small amount of filling on each leaf and roll up tightly.
Arrange the rolls snugly in a pot.
Add water, lemon juice, and olive oil, then simmer over low heat for 35 minutes.

name: Chicken Tagine
description: A sweet-and-savoury Moroccan chicken dish with apricots and almonds.
steps: Sear the chicken in olive oil.
Add the onion and spices and sauté for a few minutes.
Add the apricots and a little water, cover, and cook for 35 minutes.
Scatter with toasted almonds and serve.

name: Couscous Salad
description: A light and refreshing Moroccan couscous salad.
steps: Pour hot water over the couscous, let it stand, then fluff with a fork.
Dice the cucumber and tomato.
Combine the couscous with the vegetables and chopped mint.
Season with lemon juice, olive oil, and salt, then serve.

name: Harira Soup
description: A spiced Moroccan soup of lentils and chickpeas.
steps: Sauté the onion and celery in olive oil.
Add the tomato, lentils, chickpeas, and spices, then pour in water.
Simmer over low heat for 30 minutes.
Whisk the flour with a little water and stir in to thicken, then serve.

name: Zaalouk
description: A spiced Moroccan relish of aubergine and tomato.
steps: Cube the aubergine and boil or roast until soft.
Cook with tomato and garlic in olive oil.
Mash the aubergine in as you stir.
Season with cumin, chili flakes, and salt, then serve cold.

name: Moroccan Carrot Salad
description: Boiled carrot salad seasoned with cumin and cinnamon.
steps: Slice the carrots and boil until tender.
Toss with lemon juice, cumin, and cinnamon.
Add the olive oil and chopped parsley.
Serve warm or chilled.
